title: HighProbabilityStationarity.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective is differentiable on a second-countable real Hilbert space and may be nonconvex. Its gradient is globally L-Lipschitz, its infimum f⋆ is finite, and f(x₀) − f⋆ ≤ Δ. The infimum may be unattained.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns one vector g(x,ω) using a fresh IID seed. The map g is jointly measurable and E[g(x,ω)] = ∇f(x) at every x. The public inputs include x₀, L, σ, Δ, ε, and δ. The objective, g, the seed law, and f⋆ are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighProbabilityStationarity.lean, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: At every query point, E[‖g(x,ω) − ∇f(x)‖²] ≤ σ². This uniform centered second-moment bound permits heavy-tailed errors and includes σ = 0.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns one measurable E-valued point X. Success requires ‖∇f(X)‖ ≤ ε for ε > 0.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy the gradient-norm bound with probability at least 1 − δ for every 0 < δ ≤ 1/4, under the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness and within the fixed oracle-call budget.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighProbabilityStationarity.lean, spec.successful and spec.valid. LongTails/Template.lean, OracleTemplate.Convergence and OracleTemplate.executeWithTrace

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: First-order stationarity for a lower-bounded smooth nonconvex objective under an unbiased, bounded-variance stochastic gradient oracle is a standard benchmark. This formulation asks for a single point at a prescribed confidence level in a real Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
High-Probability Stationarity in Stochastic Optimization

We seek an approximately stationary point of a possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is Lipschitz, and the objective gap at a given starting point is bounded relative to the finite infimum of f. At each query, the oracle uses a fresh independent sample from a common distribution to return an unbiased gradient estimate with uniformly bounded variance. For tolerance ε>0 and failure probability 0<δ≤1/4, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε with probability at least 1−δ.

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). Equip E with its Borel σ-algebra and write ∥⋅∥ for its Hilbert norm. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0∈E, the smoothness constant L>0, the noise bound σ≥0, the initial gap bound Δ≥0, and the accuracy parameters ε and δ.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is Fréchet differentiable on E, and its gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E. The infimum f⋆=infx∈Ef(x) is finite and satisfies f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Stochastic gradient oracle). On call k, a query at any x∈E returns g(x,ξk), where g:E×Ω→E is jointly measurable. The samples (ξk)k≥0 are independent random variables with common law ν on Ω, and the sample sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. For every x∈E and ξ∼ν, the estimate g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable, its squared error ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and satisfy P(∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε)≥1−δ, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples.

comparisonHtml:
Let f be differentiable and bounded below on a complete, second-countable real inner-product space with its Borel σ-algebra. Assume ∇f is L-Lipschitz and f(x0)−inff≤Δ. The jointly measurable stochastic-gradient oracle uses IID samples, with mean ∇f(x) and mean squared error at most σ2 at each x. The target is one measurable point x^ satisfying Pr(∥∇f(x^)∥≤ε)≥1−δ, where L,ε>0, Δ,σ≥0, and 0<δ≤1/4.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HighProbabilityStationarity

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  δ : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧ 0 < q.δ ∧ q.δ ≤ 1 / 4
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω))
      (fstar : ℝ),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, x) ω => g x ω } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x, fstar ≤ f x) ∧ (∀ η, 0 < η → ∃ x, f x < fstar + η) ∧ f q.x0 - fstar ≤ q.Δ ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂p = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂p ≤ q.σ ^ 2)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      1 - q.δ ≤ (P : Measure _).real {ω | ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ≤ q.ε}

end LongTails.Setups.HighProbabilityStationarity
